subject.title: [Feature]: Stop Burying Your Agent's Soul: Configurable Context File Elevation

question: Should per-file bootstrap elevation and Project Context exclusion be accepted as a core typed config surface, or should this be solved through a documented plugin/context-engine contract?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the durable API changes prompt authority, prompt-cache stability, and the public config/plugin boundary, which requires maintainer product intent.

options.title: Extend plugin/context-engine contract
options.body: Document or add the minimal hook/context-engine API needed for external packages to elevate and exclude bootstrap files without another core config knob.

options.title: Add narrow core config
options.body: Accept a typed core config for ordered pattern-to-section elevation with explicit exclusion behavior, plus schema, docs, and regression tests.

options.title: Keep flat Project Context
options.body: Leave the current flat rendering behavior and direct users to existing hooks, context-engine plugins, or manual prompt additions.

recommendation.title: Extend plugin/context-engine contract
recommendation.body: Document or add the minimal hook/context-engine API needed for external packages to elevate and exclude bootstrap files without another core config knob.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter provided the latest maintainer-side framing for this exact core config versus plugin/context-engine product choice.
